title.en: A Tale of Valour: Major Somnath Sharma and the Battle of Badgam

text.en: On Republic Day we honour the brave with awards. India's first Param Vir Chakra went to Major Somnath Sharma.

Major Somnath Sharma was the first recipient of the Param Vir Chakra, India's highest gallantry award.
The events began in August 1947 when Pakistan launched Operation Gulmarg to take Kashmir, breaking its commitment to Maharaja Hari Singh.
Around 1000 invaders trained and equipped by the Pakistani Army, with deep knowledge of mountain passes and the terrain, entered the Valley.
Major Sharma and his men were sent to protect the Srinagar airport from falling into the invaders' hands.
The battle at Badgam took place on a cold November day in 1947, and the brave men held the position against heavy odds.
His courage and sacrifice protected the integrity of India's borders, and he remains an inspiration.
We remember such heroes at the National War Memorial and on Republic Day.
Valour means great courage in the face of danger, and a tribute is an act of respect.
Vocabulary: etched means fixed permanently, annex means to take possession of, and valiant means brave.
The text is a narrative of real events, so it gives dates, places and facts in order.

problem.en: Why was the Srinagar airport important?

text.en: Reinforcements could reach Kashmir by air.
If it fell, the invaders could cut help.
So Major Sharma's company defended it.

He defended Srinagar airport at Badgam in 1947.
